lines: I am watching the shallows by this road. One of mine walked out into the basin, and he has not come back.

infos.prompt: What are you waiting for here?
lines: I wait for Sei-Wan, my kin. He walked out into the basin alone, to prove himself to the Agaceph, and he has not come back.
I am Agaceph too. By our custom none of us may follow a walk-out, so I stay by this road. An outsider may follow him.

He went out east, a long way past the houses, and he is out among the trees there. Vipers lie out there. Nothing that walks in the basin lives long. Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden, keeps watch near this road and will say the same.
I want him alive. He wants the walk-out to count, and it counts only if he comes home on his own feet. If another brings him in, the Agaceph will say he did not finish.
I would have him alive and shamed sooner than proud and dead. Bring him home if you must. But if he can walk, let the walk-out be his own.

infos.prompt: Sei-Wan is alive. He is coming home.
lines: Alive. Then I can breathe again. I have stood by this road for days, and I asked for nothing more than that.
I am sorry that he has lost his walk-out. He went into the basin for it, and now he has lost it. He will not thank me, and I will bear that.
Here is sixty gold. It is not a price for him, only what I have.
No word of Sei-Wan yet. I stand by this road and watch the shallows.
By our custom I may not follow him, so I wait. He walked out alone, and he will come when he comes, on his own feet. I have to believe that.
Sei-Wan lives. That is enough for me, whatever the Agaceph say.
I am sorry that he has lost his walk-out. I asked you to bring him home, and I do not blame you. But he went into the basin for that proof, and the tribe will not count it now.

infos.prompt: Haj-Wan sent me to find you.
lines: So Haj-Wan sent an outsider. I am Sei-Wan. I walked out alone, and I was on my way home when a viper struck at me.
It lies out among the trees south-west of me. I climbed up here, and I carry nothing that can reach it.
I will not come down while it lives. I will not run past it, and I will not call for help.
If you can deal with the viper, I can walk.

infos.prompt: (Persuade) Sei-Wan, come home now. Your kin is waiting.
lines: You say it well, and I cannot answer it. Haj-Wan has waited for me, and I knew she would. I climbed up here knowing it.
I will come home. I will come in my own time, not at your heels like a hatchling led by the hand.
But I will not count the walk-out as mine. I went out to come back alone, and a viper stopped me, and a stranger cleared my road. Tell Haj-Wan I am coming, and that I am ashamed.

infos.prompt: (Persuade) Sei-Wan, come home now. Your kin is waiting.
lines: No. I walked out alone, and I will walk home alone. I will not be talked home like a hatchling.
Find words that I believe, and I may listen. Or leave the walk to me, and say so plainly. I would hear that.

infos.prompt: The viper is dead. Walk home on your own feet when you choose; I will say nothing of you, not even to Haj-Wan.
lines: Then the walk-out is still mine. I did not think an outsider would leave it to me. I am glad of it, and I am proud.
I will walk in on my own feet when I choose. My tribe will see me do it.
I ask one thing. Say nothing to the others, not of the viper and not of the trees. I know Haj-Wan will watch the shallows a little longer for me, and I am sorry for that.
The walk-out is mine, and I finish it. I come in when I choose.
You have done what I asked of you, and I will not forget it.
I said I would come, and I will, in my own time. Not at your heels.
I will not thank you. The walk-out was to be mine, and now it is not. I will finish it alone, in my own time.

infos.prompt: Will you stop me going out into the basin?
lines: No. I keep watch here, and what a tribe does with its own young is for that tribe to do. The levy has never stood in the way of a rite, and I will not stand in your way.
Sei-Wan went out into the basin days ago, and he is not back. Haj-Wan, who waits near this road, will tell you why he went.
If you go after him, I will not stop you. But hear this. What lies out among the trees bites, and what it bites dies. The levy will not come in after you, so you go alone.
I do not like what the rite costs. I watch young ones walk out here and I do not follow, because the levy keeps to this road. When one does not come back, I have stood here and watched.

infos.prompt: Haj-Wan sent me to find you.
lines: So Haj-Wan sent you, and the viper lies dead among the trees. It does not move. I would not have believed it.
My legs are stiff from the climb, but they will carry me now. I can walk.
Haj-Wan wants me home, and I will not guess what you want. What do you mean to do with me?
